title: Officers cleared in shooting deaths
article: Police involved in the fatal shootings of two people have been cleared of any wrongdoing by the Special Investigations Unit.
In the first incident, a 17-year-old was killed by an officer during an armed robbery of a sporting goods store Dec. 31.
SIU director James Cornish said in a statement that the officer had "a reasonably held belief that shooting was necessary" to preserve the officer's life and the safety of those in the area.
In the second incident, Ucal Lauzon, 34, was shot by a Toronto police officer May 27 shortly after fatally stabbing his sister, Pandora Whyte, and seriously wounding his niece, Marcia Whyte, 15.
"The involved officers had ample reason to believe that Mr. Lauzon was a dangerous person," Cornish said.
Police were called to a townhouse after Lauzon refused to leave his sister's home, where they found the niece outside with serious stab wounds.
Officers entered the home and saw Lauzon holding the knife close to the injured woman, according to the agency.
Officers drew their guns and ordered Lauzon to drop his knife but he turned towards police, the report said.
One officer fired twice, striking Lauzon. He died later in hospital.
